x: Built Develop the world from its beginning to the present age (BWM, WT). Interconnection gives immersion and a semblance of realism. Layers. An initial layer is established and the next is built on it: star → cloud → planets → moons and belts → clocks → geology → atmosphere → surface → hydrology → conditions for life → life → history of life (or created life) → peoples → states → realms and settlements → lore → languages and names. Each layer reads the ones below and writes nothing back to them. The order is now enforced by the framework ( moduleOrder() , section 19 ). Requirements. A system can develop only if its necessities are met. Life runs only where the conditions hold. Farming is found only on fertile ground. A technology is found only once its prerequisites are held. A sapient mind needs a body, a diet and a life that can pay for it. Procedural and guided. With nothing given, everything comes from a seed. With presets and locks, the rest is generated around what was fixed, and the record says which is which ( provenance ). The same seed with the same options always gives the same result. Designations, not words. The simulation identifies things by reference ( S1.P3.C2.R7 for a place, B1.L17.Pδ for a population of a lineage). Names are given afterwards, by the peoples who live there, in their own languages. Looked into on demand. The whole world is known coarsely, and detail is made only where it is wanted. Judgements are marked. Every specification separates what is measured or derived from physics from what is a judgement. Data, not code. Traits, niches, coevolution pairs, technologies, races, religion, magic, law, beings, sound laws, body plans, naming styles, climate bands, game profiles, variants and message catalogues are JSON files.

Partial 3.1 What Demiurge does Eons of the planet ( Solar System §12.4): Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic, with boundaries set by events. Aeons of the history of life ( Solar System §20.7g; Additions §4): numbered by the breaks in the history of life, with the Aeon that begins with the primary radiation named the Phanerozoic . Eras divide it at mass extinctions of 40 % or more of the lineages. Periods, Epochs and Ages are cut by what happens. The further eons, built ( Additions §4): Hysterozoic ("Later Life") after a dying of nine lineages in ten (Eras: Protozoic, Deuterozoic, Tritozoic, then ordinals); Necrogean ("Dead World") when the biosphere is lost; Xenozoic ("Foreign Life") as the first Aeon after an introduced origin of life. The triggers are judgements. Models ( Generate §2): simple (four planets, no belts or comets, no disturbance beyond the planet’s own), standard (the default) and advanced (the planet’s future followed two billion years further, so that a great dying can end the Phanerozoic and begin the Hysterozoic). These are the nearest the modules support to BWM’s and WT’s simple, standard and advanced models. Cultural time : steps of a century, until the present rule stops it ( section 12 ).

Built Solar System §9, §12.1, §19. The table of version 1 stands: accretion, core, first crust, bombardment, outgassing, oceans, continents, plate tectonics that begin, rift, weld and end, supercontinents detected rather than scripted, relief from the plates, and the magnetic field. New: the history of life now has asteroid impacts , large igneous provinces and glaciations as disturbances ( Evolution to Sapience – Build Notes ). Each acts as a mass event in the biosphere’s record. The Creation ( section 18 ) keeps a world’s plates and land but remakes its air and sea in an instant ( terraform() ). Still to build Erosion, and ice ages in the map The land does not change once made (framework gap). The glaciations of the biology module lower the sea in the biosphere’s own record , not in the map, so there are no ice sheets, land bridges or sea-level changes on the map itself.

Built Geography and Polity Module – Specification §1; Landmarks and Water Features – Specification §1. Zones from a lattice of 25 km² tiles in 15 kinds of ground; rivers divide the ground; barrier zones; habitability; subzones. Unchanged from version 1. Landmarks ( landmarksOf ), built : peaks, volcanoes (active or dormant, with hot springs and geysers), great rivers, deltas, waterfalls, gorges, great and salt lakes, glaciers, cave systems (karst and lava tubes), craters (by the age of the surface, kept or lost by rain and relief), straits, bays, great deserts and plains. Each has a hazard (what it can do to the people about it) and an awe (how likely a people is to hold it sacred), which religion and myth read. Natural disasters acting on peoples , built in the culture module: eruptions, earthquakes, floods and storms by the ground ( section 12 ). Still to build Names of landmarks, and land bridges Landmarks are not yet named. Land bridges and migration barriers are used in the history of life but not labelled on the map. Sea-floor features (trenches, seamounts) are zones of the sea but not landmarks.

Partial Solar System §20; Niches – Specification ; Evolution to Sapience – Outline (v0.2) and Build Notes . Traits : 164 (was 109), now including the life-history, cognitive, plant, pollination, fruit, grass, parasitic, eusocial and manipulator traits of the Outline. Niches : 59 templates (was 42). Coevolution : 28 pairs in data/coevolution.json (arms races and mutualisms; Outline §3.2). Niche construction : engineer niches generalised. Life history : the axes lifespan, juvenile period, diet quality, vocal, insulation, crypsis and detox. Fecundity falls as lifespan rises, and generation time and recovery follow. Feedback : wood burial and lignin decay on oxygen; the fire regime. Disturbance : impacts, large igneous provinces, glaciations. During tuning, survival rules were added (a mass event spares numerous, widespread lineages more often, and one refuge lineage survives for each great group). Running time : followed to a mind, steps of 4 Myr with 140 lineages kept, falling to 1 Myr near a mind and 200 kyr after tool use. Relations ( relations.ts ), built : pollination, seed dispersal, parasitism, symbiosis and disease, derived from the living lineages. Bestiary ( bestiary.ts ), built : "the creatures of this forest", the living creatures by the cover of their places, read by the RPG conversion and by anyone presenting a biome. Classification is as in version 1: no fixed categories, rank earned by divergence, groups recorded by designation. Still to build Run-based checks of the feedbacks The Outline’s §10.2 tests that need whole runs are not written: oxygen rising with forests and falling after lignin decay, the fire gate in a run, forbid honoured, and the order of events against Earth’s.

Partial Evolution to Sapience – Outline §6–8; Build Notes . Built: WT’s intellect tree as a chain of traits: spatial memory, extended juvenile period, long lifespan, cooperative breeding, social cognition, vocal apparatus and learning, causal reasoning, mental simulation (Imagination), tool use, cultural transmission, fine motor control, tool manufacture, fire use, cooking, cumulative culture, sapience. Tool use needs a manipulator (hand, arms, trunk, beak or mandibles). Gates: large_brain needs diet quality ≥ 0.4 and a body of 30 g or more. sapience needs cumulative culture, land, a population (log N ≥ 4) and a body of 500 g or more. fire_use needs a fire regime. cultural_transmission needs a life of 10 years or more. The hand-off ( SapienceHandoff ), built : body, cradle, body plan for speech, domesticates, crops, fauna, flora, dangers, disease burden and relations, read by the culture module ( speciesFromHandoff ). Measured once: of 24 Earth-like worlds with an animal explosion, 6 reached sapience (about a quarter), at 293–1 303 Myr after the primary radiation (Earth: 539). Eight more got part of the way. About half never got a large brain.

Race Mass Life Cold limit Notes Human 65 kg 70 y 8 °C the reference; river plains and temperate lowlands Dwarf 80 kg 200 y −4 °C mountains and underground; builders and smiths Elf 55 kg 400 y −4 °C old forests; slow breeding; keen senses; mana_sensitive Orc 90 kg 50 y −10 °C fast breeding, hardy, warlike Troll 280 kg 120 y −18 °C the cold high country; intellect 0.85 Ogre 250 kg 90 y −8 °C heavy, in small clans; intellect 0.8 Sentient monsters ( data/races/monsters.json , proposals): Goblins, Fishmen, Giants . Several races in one world , built : each species founds peoples where it is at home, and peoples of different species compete for land but do not assimilate or blend. A state ruling another species leaves it a substrate. Daughter cultures keep their mother’s species. Subraces , built : cultures of one species grouped by their land (highland, northern, tropical, desert, coastal, forest, steppe, riverine, lowland), with bodies shifted by Bergmann’s and Allen’s rules. Still to build Per-race hand-offs, aquatic and subterranean peoples The hand-off’s domesticates, dangers and disease burden are judged against the first race only (human by default; Two Defaults §1). A troll ought to keep different beasts. Fishmen are modelled as a land people of the shores, because there is no aquatic way of life . Dwarves prefer underground but have no subterranean way of life . 11.2 Monsters, beasts and beings Beasts : the bestiary of the biology module (evolved worlds) or the created species (the Creation), converted to creature statistics. Constructs and spirits ( beings.ts ), built : golems, automata, guardians and illusions in great ruins and colleges of magic; ghosts at great calamities and battles; elementals at hot spots; spirits of place and ancestors' shades at sacred places. Without magic they are tales only.

Partial Language Module – Specification ; Morphology Outline ; Naming Outline ; Melodic Channel ; Writing, Sound Change and Descent . Phonetics, morphology, names and piped languages as in version 1. New, all built: Vocabulary : 371 concepts (was 316). The gaps against WT’s core lexicon are filled: sky, day, season, year, past, future and the seasons; kin; offices (ruler, warrior, priest, smith …); craft (tool, weapon, bow …); lore (writing, law, magic, spell, curse, omen …). Sound change : 32 laws as operations on features, drawn in proportion to time; borrowing fitted to the borrower’s sounds. Descent : a tree of languages following the tree of cultures. Daughters inherit, blends mix, rulers and ruled exchange words by the contact’s influence, and different species do not borrow. Writing systems : the type follows learning (tallies, pictographs, logographic, syllabary, alphabet, abugida, abjad) and the language’s shape. The medium gives tool, style and direction. A piped language is written as notation. Charts of signs. Still to build Syntax, the Eventide sound laws, the evolved people's language Syntax is not built (word order, noun phrases, relative clauses, phrases beyond one inflected verb). The Eventide sound laws (great consonant shift, a-merger, rhotacism) are not yet written as data in the variant, nor is the Avya composite script. The evolved people’s founding language reads its body plan in the wiki export, but wiring the hand-off’s body plan into buildLanguage is the last step still open. Still missing: allophony, suppletion, numerals and classifiers, family names, tonogenesis, epenthesis and metathesis, the full lexicon.

x: Built; needs review The Two Defaults – Implementation Notes ; Generate §1. The Creation ( generic-fantasy , the default) The naturalistic route ( sci-fi ) Variant ( variant:eventide ) Cosmos any star and planets. A main world is accepted if it can be remade: rocky, 0.4–2.5 Earth masses, not tidally locked (up to 30 systems tried) physics only; up to 400 systems tried for a world with animal life as the Creation The world remade Earth-like in an instant : Earth’s air, mean 288 K, liquid water, about 30 % land; its own plates and land as it is as the Creation Life created , not evolved: species fitted to each niche of a finished world, drawn from the trait tree evolved to a mind : plain histories, then guided, then a last resort that promotes the lineage furthest up the chain created Peoples Humans, Dwarves, Elves, Orcs, Trolls, Ogres, Goblins, Fishmen, Giants , each where it is at home the evolved species, one people in its cradle the variant’s races Magic medium none medium Lost civilisation and myth emergent and ancient; divine frame (the creator "made the world whole in a single act") emergent; cultural frame as the Creation History ends at iron, writing and the castle (at most 20 000 years) after the span; run again longer if no state and writing arose, else the next world as the Creation A world in either default is accepted only with at least 40 million km² of land and 25 million km² of mild, wet land. 18.1 Custom variants Built ( Variants and Races §2–3). A variant is a folder data/variants/<id>/ with a manifest, races, phonology and morphology presets, naming styles and an RPG profile. The defaults never read it. A variant’s races replace the defaults. Command lines take --variant NAME ; generate takes --mode variant:<id> . Eventide is the first variant: races (human, hynral, doari, tulkata, hadur, karaqa, with IE’s tables kept for checking), the five language presets, three morphology presets, the troll naming style, and the Eventide RPG profile and skills. That this is all data, with no change to the modules' code, is the test of the system, and test/variants.test.ts checks it. In generate , Eventide uses the Creation with its own races, and the first race (human) is the body the hand-off is judged against.

19.1 The module framework Built ( src/framework.ts ). MODULES describes each module once: status, what it requires and provides, its lockable options, specification, entry function, and its open gaps . moduleOrder() orders them and refuses a circle or a missing module. describeFramework() prints the table. Locks fix any option whatever the mode sets ( generate({ locks: { 'solar.starMass': 1, 'lore.magic': 'low' } }) ), and the plan’s provenance records each. Progress is reported by stage, and by step inside the biology and culture modules. 19.2 Localisation Partial ( src/i18n.ts , data/i18n/ ). The frame covers the 14 locales (British English and French, German, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Persian, Hindi, Armenian, Georgian, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean), each with its direction (Persian right to left), script, and the romanisation to use for generated languages. It offers t(locale, key, vars) with English fall-back, number formatting and plural categories. Still to build Translated catalogues The only catalogue is the headings of the wiki export , in all 14 locales, and the 13 translations are drafts for a native speaker to review . The module reports still write English directly. Romanising generated languages into each locale’s script is still to do. Still to build Speed The history of life is the dominant cost. A profiling pass on the per-step web and selection kernels (or a port to WebAssembly, as the solar-system specification allows) is suggested before the sci-fi route is usable interactively.
